newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico March preliminary trade surplus $565 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico March preliminary trade surplus $565 mln.

text.p: Mexico's March preliminary trade surplus was $565 million, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
Exports were $8.732 billion, a rise of 14.7 percent compared to March 1996, it said.
Imports were $8.167 billion in March, a rise of 19.4 percent compard to March 1996, it added.
The Finance Ministry said the surplus was the highest in the last six months.
In the first quarter of the year the accumulated surplus was $1.348 billion.
In the first quarter accumulated exports were $24.865 billion, 13.7 percent higher than the same period a year earlier.
Accumulated imports rose 18.0 percent in the first quarter compared to the first quarter last year to $23.517 billion, the ministry said.
Imports in March of intermediate goods were $6.56 billion, 18.7 percent higher than in March a year before.
Imports of capital goods in March were $994 million, 23.6 percent higher than in March a year before.
Imports of consumer goods were $613 million, 20.7 percent than in the same month a year earlier.
Exports of manufactured goods rose 15.6 percent in March to $7.221 billion, it said.
March exports of petroleum products were 8.9 percent higher over the year to $957 million.
Agricultural products exports rose 14.0 percent in March to $521 million.
Mining products exports were $33 million in March, it said.
In March exports of manufactruing products made up 82.7 percent of the total, petroleum products 10.9 percent, agricultural products 6.0 percent and mining 0.4 percent, the ministry said.
